periods.analysis: 311 feed shows 91.4% of utility service requests closed within SLA in 2024-Q3, with priorValue null and delta null because this is the first quarter in this run. That is green against the >=90% target, and the North Beach valve-box backlog cleanup plus the Route 6 hydrant-ticket sweep helped keep the queue from getting stale. Useful anomaly: after Labor Day, sewer-odor calls spiked near Harborview Station, but the U-2 customer response crew still closed most same-day—nice save 👍.
periods.recommendations: Keep the daily 8:15 a.m. 311 exception huddle and extend the Route 6 sweep checklist to Route 9 before the first fall storm. Also tag Harborview Station odor calls as a mini-cohort in Cityworks so we can see repeat locations fast and not lose SLA time chasing duplicates.

periods.analysis: 2024-Q4 improved to 92.1%, up 0.7 points from 91.4%, per the 311 feed. Still green, and the holiday coverage grid for the Westside utility desk looks like it worked—fewer tickets sat over 48 hours even with permit-inspection handoffs around the Marina Loop. The chronological story is good so far: we did not just clear a one-quarter backlog, we held the rhythm into a messier quarter.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the holiday coverage grid as the standard Q4 playbook and pre-load backup assignees for Marina Loop and Old Pier Road tickets. Please keep the 311-to-Cityworks status sync audit every Friday; it is boring, but it is exactly how we avoid stale-number drama.

periods.analysis: 2025-Q1 came in at 90.1%, down 2.0 points from 92.1%, but still green and just above the >=90% target. The dip lines up with January rain events and a heavier water-main call cohort on Bayview Drive, especially around asset WM-18-441 where restoration tickets needed extra dispatch touches. Not panicking—this is still a pass—but it is the first watch item in the arc because the margin got thin.
periods.recommendations: Keep the result green by adding a temporary Q1 rain-event triage code in the 311 feed and routing Bayview Drive repeat calls directly to the U-4 water distribution lead. Extend the SLA aging dashboard to flag tickets at 75% of allowed time, not just when they breach, so crews get a real early nudge.

periods.analysis: 2025-Q2 rebounded to 91.7%, up 1.6 points from 90.1%, back to a healthier green cushion. The Pipeline Renewal coordination helped here: when valve isolation work on Seacliff Avenue generated resident calls, the pre-scripted 311 responses and Alpha Paving restoration slots kept closures moving. The main thing I noticed is that permit-related utility tickets no longer dragged the average like they did in Q1—good operational cleanup.
periods.recommendations: Keep using the Pipeline Renewal call scripts for any planned shutdown over four hours, and add the Seacliff Avenue template to the 311 knowledge base permanently. Also expand the 75% SLA aging flag to permit-restoration tickets assigned to vendors, since that cohort is where handoffs can quietly slip.

periods.analysis: 2025-Q3 rose again to 93.3%, up 1.6 points from 91.7%, the best result in this sequence so far. Green is solid here, and the summer Rapid Closeout pilot on beach-area service requests—especially Route 2 meters, hydrants, and low-pressure calls—looks like it paid off. Tiny flag nobody asked for: weekend tickets closed faster, but Monday re-open rates ticked up around short-paved cuts, so speed and quality both need eyes.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the Rapid Closeout pilot and make Route 2 the training example for the other coastal routes before next summer. Add a Monday re-open review for short-paved restoration tickets with Harbor Asphalt so the higher SLA close rate does not create avoidable second touches.

periods.analysis: 2025-Q4 eased to 92.0%, down 1.3 points from 93.3%, still green and still comfortably above target. The drop is not surprising after the Q3 high: November king tides and two after-hours water-main responses near Cedar Quay pushed more tickets into supervisor review before closure. The serious water-main issue is being actively managed through Pipeline Renewal, and the SLA number says customer follow-through is holding even while the infrastructure work is noisy.
periods.recommendations: Keep Pipeline Renewal resident-notification blocks tied to 311 ticket categories, especially for Cedar Quay and East Harbor pressure complaints. Extend the after-hours supervisor review roster by one backup lead during king-tide weeks so closure approvals do not wait until the next business morning.

periods.analysis: 2026-Q1 is 91.8%, down 0.2 points from 92.0%, which is basically flat and still green. That is a steady handoff from the busier Q4, with winter leak calls on Inland Route 4 absorbed by the same-day utility desk and the Neptune Pump Station complaint cluster closed without an SLA slide. On it 👍—the trend says the process is durable, not just lucky, as long as we keep watching water-main-driven volume.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the same-day utility desk through the end of the wet season and keep Inland Route 4 on the daily crew board until leak-call volume normalizes. Add Neptune Pump Station complaint IDs to the weekly 311 exception export so repeat callers are grouped before dispatch, not after.

periods.analysis: 92.4% of service requests closed within SLA in June, 2.4 points above the 90% target and a modest improvement on May's 91.8%. Misses remain concentrated in the same two categories as prior months: sidewalk and curb repair requests that require a joint inspection with Streets, and hydrant flow-test follow-ups that queue behind scheduled main flushing. Neither category is resource-constrained so much as sequencing-constrained — both wait on a second crew's calendar rather than on Public Works capacity.
periods.recommendations: Establish a standing weekly joint-inspection window with Streets to clear the sidewalk and curb queue on a predictable cadence instead of ad hoc scheduling. Reclassify hydrant flow-test follow-ups with an SLA that reflects the flushing schedule, so the measure tracks a commitment the division can actually control. Both changes are process-only and can be in place before the Q1 FY27 review.

periods.analysis: SLA closure finished the quarter at 88.6% against a 90% target — the first miss in eight quarters. The shortfall is concentrated in the Maple St corridor, where the water main incident in late July generated 412 unplanned service requests in nine days. Those tickets carried a median age of 6.1 days against a 3.4-day baseline, and they alone account for roughly 1.8 points of the gap. Excluding the incident window, closure held at 91.2%.
periods.recommendations: No structural change recommended. The corridor backlog cleared on 8/29 and weekly closure returned above 91% for the final three weeks of the quarter. Recommend holding the 90% target for Q4-26 and adding a corridor-level breakout to the Public Works performance report so incident-driven spikes are visible before they show up in the quarterly roll-up.
